gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham reads friendly and modern, with a big middle band. Nordic's stitched-thread outlines and closed shapes stand firm above it, while the body's hanging s ends loosen everything below.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, its curve endings keeping well apart from one another. Nordic's blunt, untapered strokes make the plainest partner for it.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Nordic is powerful and ancient, drawn with a flat line along every curve and brush-dab spacing between letters. Noto Sans Soyombo counters with a sizable x-height and wide, unclosed curves, which is the real strength of this sans-serif pairing.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Ancient weight comes from Nordic, whose closed, cramped letters sit far apart like brush dabs on paper. Noto Sans Sundanese has open e mouths, so give it generous size.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Nordic has no calligraphic shading at all, just one monoweight stroke. Noto Sans Sunuwar brings curves that leave daylight and short ascender stems, and that sans-serif openness is the pair's strongest quality against the heading's tight folds.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-syloti-na: Nordic opens with powerful, ancient energy, its closed letters spaced out like dabs of a brush on paper. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri answers with short ascenders and a tall x-height.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac has tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs and s shapes that turn wide and easy. Nordic, meanwhile, does its best work being closed, heavy and ancient.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Ancient and blunt, Nordic stamps out closed letters with brush-dab gaps between them. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern gives tall lowercase against small caps, and its curve endings never crowd, which makes that openness the pair's best quality.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Stark and ancient, Nordic traces one rolling-ball-pen width through every letter, spaced like brush dabs.
